citations.quote: Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$ and let $\xi$ be a clamped knot vector as in [[def-b-spline-space-and-basis]]. The recursively defined degree-$p$ B-splines are nonnegative, are supported on $[\xi_j,\xi_{j+p+1}]$, and are piecewise polynomials of degree at most $p$. At a knot of multiplicity $\mu\le p$, each B-spline is $C^{p-\mu}$; multiplicity $p+1$ imposes no continuity requirement. On every nonempty knot interval $[\xi_m,\xi_{m+1})$, the active functions $B_{m-p,p,\xi},\ldots,B_{m,p,\xi}$ form a basis of $\mathcal P_p$ and sum to one. Globally, the $n$ B-splines form a basis of $S_{p,\xi}$. In particular, every $q\in\mathcal P_p$ has a unique expansion $q=\sum_{j=1}^n c_jB_{j,p,\xi}$ on $[a,b]$.

Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let the reference patch be $\widehat\Omega=(0,1)^d$. For each coordinate $r$, fix a degree $p_r\in\mathbb N_0$, a finite clamped knot vector $\Xi_r$ on $[0,1]$, and its one-dimensional B-spline basis $B^{(r)}_{i_r,p_r,\Xi_r}$ from [[def-b-spline-space-and-basis]]. For a multi-index $\alpha=(i_1,\ldots,i_d)$ in the finite product index set $\mathcal I$, define the tensor-product basis function
$$N_\alpha(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d):=\prod_{r=1}^d B^{(r)}_{i_r,p_r,\Xi_r}(\xi_r).$$

Choose finitely many control points $P_\alpha\in\mathbb R^d$ and positive weights $w_\alpha$, and write $0<w_-:=\min_\alpha w_\alpha\le\max_\alpha w_\alpha=:w_+<\infty$. The weight denominator, rational basis, and associated rational spline space are
$$W(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}w_\alpha N_\alpha(\xi),\qquad R_\alpha(\xi):=\frac{w_\alpha N_\alpha(\xi)}{W(\xi)},\qquad \mathcal N_h:=\operatorname{span}\{R_\alpha:\alpha\in\mathcal I\}.$$
The corresponding NURBS geometry map is
$$F(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}R_\alpha(\xi)P_\alpha.$$
Equivalently, let $\widetilde F(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}(w_\alpha P_\alpha,w_\alpha)N_\alpha(\xi)\in\mathbb R^{d+1}$ and let $\Pi(y,z):=y/z$ for $z>0$. Then $F=\Pi\circ\widetilde F$ wherever $W>0$.
The basis properties in [[thm-spline-polynomial-reproduction]] give nonnegative tensor factors summing to one. Consequently the weights' convex combination satisfies $W\ge w_->0$; the later item `lem-positive-nurbs-basis-and-quotient-derivative` records the full rational-basis consequences.

An admissible NURBS patch map is a continuous, globally injective, bi-Lipschitz map $F:\overline{\widehat\Omega}\to\overline\Omega$ whose restriction to every nonempty knot cell is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism onto its image. There are constants $0<j_-\le j_+<\infty$ and $1\le L<\infty$ such that, almost everywhere on every cell,
$$j_-\le J_F:=\det DF\le j_+,\qquad \|DF\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L,\qquad \|DF^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L.$$
The physical image $\Omega$ is required to be a bounded Lipschitz domain. The images of the finite knot cells form a face-to-face partition with the piecewise $C^1$ boundary presentation of [[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]]; the map agrees on each shared cell face.

A finite multipatch geometry consists of finitely many such patch maps with disjoint physical interiors, a connected bounded Lipschitz union, and matching full physical faces wherever two patches meet. Positive weights only define a positive denominator and a convex rational basis; they do not assert global injectivity, positive Jacobian, or interface matching. Exact NURBS representation means exact representation of the specified CAD map and does not assert that this map is the exact geometry of a target physical domain.

derivations.claim: Each tensor product $N_\alpha$ is nonnegative by [F1]. On any open tensor knot cell, each coordinate lies in one nonempty knot interval, so finite distributivity and [F1] give $\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}N_\alpha(\xi)=\prod_{r=1}^d\left(\sum_{i_r}B^{(r)}_{i_r,p_r,\Xi_r}(\xi_r)\right)=1.$ Hence $0\le N_\alpha\le1$ on the cell. The endpoint values follow by the one-sided endpoint convention in [[def-b-spline-space-and-basis]].

Since every coefficient $w_\alpha$ is between $w_-$ and $w_+$, the identity in step 1.1 yields $w_-\sum_\alpha N_\alpha\le W=\sum_\alpha w_\alpha N_\alpha\le w_+\sum_\alpha N_\alpha,$ so $w_-\le W\le w_+$. Thus each $R_\alpha$ is well-defined and nonnegative, and $\sum_\alpha R_\alpha=\frac{\sum_\alpha w_\alpha N_\alpha}{W}=1.$ For any coefficients $c_\alpha$, $\sum_\alpha c_\alpha R_\alpha=(1/W)\sum_\alpha(c_\alpha w_\alpha)N_\alpha$. Multiplication of each coefficient by the nonzero $w_\alpha$ is a bijection on the finite coefficient space, so the span equals $S_h/W$.

On the open knot cell all $N_\alpha$ and $W$ are polynomial and $W\ge w_->0$ by step 2.1. The ordinary quotient rule gives the displayed gradient formula. Also $\|\nabla W\|_\infty\le\sum_\alpha w_\alpha\|\nabla N_\alpha\|_\infty\le G_W$ and $N_\alpha\le1$ by step 1.1. Applying these bounds to the quotient rule proves the stated derivative estimate. The finite number of polynomial pieces makes each $G_N$ finite.

Require $S_j\cap E$ to have surface measure zero in each face, using [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]. E contains the boundaries of the faces relative to their patches and every overlap $S_i\cap S_j$, i different from j. For a specified finite gluing also list the open pieces with disjoint interiors, the shared faces, and their opposite outward normals. Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, let
$u,v\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and let
$\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n$ be the multi-index of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]. We say that $v$ is
the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Both integrals are finite because the test and all its derivatives are bounded
and compactly supported. The test identity is choice-free. By
[[def-locally-integrable-function-as-a-regular-distribution]] and the signed
transpose convention in [[def-distributional-derivative]], it is equivalent
to $\partial^\alpha T_u=T_v$ as distributions. For $\alpha=0$, this identity
reduces to $T_u=T_v$, hence to $u=v$ almost everywhere by the published
embedding theorem under [[def-countable-choice]].

**Well-definedness.** Changing either representative on a null set leaves each
test integral unchanged. Weak derivatives are therefore statements about
almost-everywhere classes; existence and uniqueness of their locally
integrable value classes are audited separately.

derivations.claim: Fix a component $q\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$, a test function $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ and a coordinate $j$. The finite physical partition and face-equality convention are those of [F1]. On each cell $K$, the vector field $G_K:=v_q\phi e_j$ is $C^1$ up to the cell boundary. By [F3], $\int_K v_q\,\partial_j\phi+\partial_jv_q\,\phi=\int_{\partial K}v_q\phi\,n_{K,j}\,dS.$ Summing this identity over the finitely many cells is legitimate because both volume terms are integrable by the hypotheses and [F4]. On a shared face the two normal fluxes add to $(v_{q,K}-v_{q,K'})\phi n_{K,j}$, which is zero by the matching-trace assumption; edge overlaps have surface measure zero by [F2]. The exterior boundary term is zero because $\phi$ is compactly supported in $\Omega$. Therefore $\int_\Omega v_q\,\partial_j\phi=-\sum_K\int_K\partial_jv_q\,\phi.$

For every component $q$ and coordinate $j$, define $g_{qj}$ to equal the classical $\partial_jv_q$ on each open cell and arbitrarily on the cell faces. The faces have $d$-dimensional measure zero under the finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation, and the finite sum of cellwise $L^2$ norms is finite, so $g_{qj}\in L^2(\Omega)$. Step 1.1 gives the weak-derivative identity for every test function, hence $D_jv_q=g_{qj}$ weakly. Each component of $v$ is also square integrable on the finite bounded cell partition; [F4] therefore gives $v\in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$ with the asserted componentwise gradient.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p<\infty$ and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then the intersection
$$C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)\cap W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$$
is dense in $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$: for every
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and every $\delta>0$ there is a function
$v\in C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with $v\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and
$\|v-u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. No regularity of $\partial\Omega$ and no
extension of $u$ beyond $\Omega$ is assumed. The exponent $p=\infty$ is
excluded, as the companion remark records.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, let
$u,v\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and let
$\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n$ be the multi-index of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]. We say that $v$ is
the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Both integrals are finite because the test and all its derivatives are bounded
and compactly supported. The test identity is choice-free. By
[[def-locally-integrable-function-as-a-regular-distribution]] and the signed
transpose convention in [[def-distributional-derivative]], it is equivalent
to $\partial^\alpha T_u=T_v$ as distributions. For $\alpha=0$, this identity
reduces to $T_u=T_v$, hence to $u=v$ almost everywhere by the published
embedding theorem under [[def-countable-choice]].

**Well-definedness.** Changing either representative on a null set leaves each
test integral unchanged. Weak derivatives are therefore statements about
almost-everywhere classes; existence and uniqueness of their locally
integrable value classes are audited separately.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. On $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]) define $$(u,v)_{H^1}:=(u,v)_{L^2}+\sum_{i=1}^n(D_iu,D_iv)_{L^2},$$ with the $L^2$ inner product of [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. Then $(\cdot,\cdot)_{H^1}$ is an inner product on the Sobolev classes whose induced norm is the $W^{1,2}$ norm of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and $H^1(\Omega)$ is a Hilbert space for it. The zero-boundary space $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a closed subspace of $H^1(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]) and hence a Hilbert space for the restricted inner product. The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, in the convention of [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]].

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be open and let $z\in H^1(U)$ vanish almost everywhere outside a compact set $K\subset U$. Then $z\in H^1_0(U)$, where $H^1_0(U)$ is the $H^1$ closure of $C_c^\infty(U)$.

Under the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]], a finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of a nonempty bounded open $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, consists of compact faces $S_1,\ldots,S_q$ covering its boundary, each a compact Borel subset of a regular $C^1$ hypersurface patch, and a compact edge set $E\subset\partial\Omega$. Require $S_j\cap E$ to have surface measure zero in each face, using [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]. E contains the boundaries of the faces relative to their patches and every overlap $S_i\cap S_j$, i different from j. At every point outside E the domain boundary is locally a single $C^1$ graph with Omega on one side. Each face carries this actual outward unit normal off E. Values assigned to the normal on E do not affect its integral.

For a specified finite gluing also list the open pieces with disjoint interiors, the shared faces, and their opposite outward normals. Require the pieces to cover the final domain up to their boundary faces, and the exposed faces to give its specified presentation. Internal faces are counted twice before cancellation, once from each side. The phrase piecewise smooth by itself supplies none of this data.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. If Omega has the specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation and $F\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$, then $\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}F=\sum_j\int_{S_j}F\cdot\nu_j\,dS$, with faces counted once off E. All integrals are finite. In a specified finite gluing, the two fluxes on every shared face cancel.

First let $v\in C^\infty(\Omega)\cap H^1(\Omega)$. On each open knot cell the differentiability expansions of $F$ and $v$ give $
abla_\xi(v\circ F)=DF^\mathsf T(
abla_xv)\circ F$. Fix a test function compactly supported in $\widehat\Omega$. Its support stays away from the exterior patch boundary. On every part of a cell where the test function is nonzero, its image under $F$ lies in a compact subset of $\Omega$, so $v\circ F$ and its first derivatives are bounded there; near exterior faces the test function vanishes. Apply the divergence theorem [F6] to $(v\circ F)\phi e_j$ cell by cell. The values of $v\circ F$ and $\phi$ agree on either side of every shared face, so opposite normal fluxes cancel, and exterior terms vanish. This proves the weak-derivative identity without requiring $v$ to extend to $\partial\Omega$. Cellwise change of variables [F2], summed over the finite partition using finite additivity of the integral, yields $\|v\circ F\|_{L^2(\widehat\Omega)}^2\le j_-^{-1}\|v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2,\qquad \|
abla_\xi(v\circ F)\|_{L^2(\widehat\Omega)}^2\le L^2j_-^{-1}\|
abla_xv\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2.$ Thus $\|v\circ F\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)}\le j_-^{-1/2}\sqrt{1+L^2}\|v\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$. The same argument applied to $F^{-1}$, whose Jacobian is $J_F^{-1}$ and derivative is bounded by $L$, gives the reverse estimate.

For arbitrary $u\in H^1(\Omega)$, choose $v_n\in C^\infty(\Omega)\cap H^1(\Omega)$ with $v_n\to u$ in $H^1$ by [F1]. Step 1.1 applied to $v_n-v_m$ makes $v_n\circ F$ Cauchy in $H^1(\widehat\Omega)$; completeness [F4] gives a limit $\widehat u\in H^1(\widehat\Omega)$. The same change-of-variables estimate in step 1.1 implies $v_n\circ F\to u\circ F$ in $L^2(\widehat\Omega)$, so this limit is the composition class. The gradient formula follows by taking the $L^2$ limit of the step 1.1 gradients: the bound on $DF$ and the change-of-variables estimate imply $DF^\mathsf T(\nabla v_n)\circ F\to DF^\mathsf T(\nabla u)\circ F$ in $L^2$. Repeating the argument with $F^{-1}$ proves the reverse estimate and inverse pullback.

Suppose $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ and choose $\varphi_n\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ converging to $u$ in $H^1$ by [F4]. Each $\varphi_n\circ F$ belongs to $H^1(\widehat\Omega)$ by step 1.1 and has compact support in $\widehat\Omega$, because $F^{-1}$ maps compact subsets of $\Omega$ to compact subsets of $\widehat\Omega$. Applying [F5] gives $\varphi_n\circ F\in H^1_0(\widehat\Omega)$. The forward estimate in step 2.1 gives convergence in $H^1$, and closedness in [F4] implies $u\circ F\in H^1_0(\widehat\Omega)$. Applying the same reasoning to $F^{-1}$ proves the converse. Finally, the scalar energy identity follows by substituting $
abla_xu\circ F=DF^{-\mathsf T}
abla_\xi\widehat u$ and $dx=J_F\,d\xi$ into the defining integral. For a vector field with row-gradient convention, $
abla_xv=(
abla_\xi\widehat v)DF^{-1}$; hence $\varepsilon_x(v)\circ F=\operatorname{sym}((
abla_\xi\widehat v)DF^{-1})$ and $\operatorname{div}_xv\circ F=\operatorname{tr}((
abla_\xi\widehat v)DF^{-1})$, which gives the stated elasticity transformation.

and every $L^p$ component norm is preserved:

$$C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)\cap W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$$
is dense in $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$: for every

Every open cover of $\Omega$ admits an at most countable locally finite smooth partition of unity with compact supports, each support contained in some cover member. $n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of

Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$, $n\ge p+1$, and $a<b$. A clamped knot vector is a nondecreasing finite sequence
$$\xi_1=\cdots=\xi_{p+1}=a<\xi_{p+2}\le\cdots\le\xi_n<\xi_{n+1}=\cdots=\xi_{n+p+1}=b,$$
with $\xi_j<\xi_{j+p+1}$ for every $1\le j\le n$. Empty interior ranges are omitted. The multiplicity $\mu(\eta)$ of an interior knot $\eta$ is its number of occurrences among $\xi_{p+2},\ldots,\xi_n$.

Write $\mathcal P_p$ for the real polynomials of degree at most $p$. The degree-$p$ spline space $S_{p,\xi}$ consists of functions that restrict to a member of $\mathcal P_p$ on each nonempty knot interval and whose derivatives through order $p-\mu(\eta)$ agree across each interior knot $\eta$. The convention $C^{-1}$ means that no matching condition is imposed. For this piecewise definition, take knot cells left-closed and right-open; at a knot with no matching condition, the value is the one from the cell on its right, and at $b$ use the left limit. Thus the function value at a discontinuous knot is specified.

For each degree $d\in\{0,\ldots,p\}$, the functions $B_{j,d,\xi}$ are indexed by $1\le j\le n+p-d$. Set
$$B_{j,0,\xi}(x)=\mathbf 1_{[\xi_j,\xi_{j+1})}(x),\qquad 1\le j\le n+p.$$
For $1\le d\le p$ and $1\le j\le n+p-d$, define recursively
$$B_{j,d,\xi}(x)=\frac{x-\xi_j}{\xi_{j+d}-\xi_j}B_{j,d-1,\xi}(x)+\frac{\xi_{j+d+1}-x}{\xi_{j+d+1}-\xi_{j+1}}B_{j+1,d-1,\xi}(x),$$
where a term with zero denominator is defined to be zero. For every degree $d$ and every allowed index $j$, set $B_{j,d,\xi}(b)$ equal to its left limit. In particular, the degree-$p$ family has indices $1\le j\le n$. Its basis and regularity properties are proved in [[thm-spline-polynomial-reproduction]].

Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$ and let $\xi$ be a clamped knot vector as in [[def-b-spline-space-and-basis]]. The recursively defined degree-$p$ B-splines are nonnegative, are supported on $[\xi_j,\xi_{j+p+1}]$, and are piecewise polynomials of degree at most $p$. At a knot of multiplicity $\mu\le p$, each B-spline is $C^{p-\mu}$; multiplicity $p+1$ imposes no continuity requirement. On every nonempty knot interval $[\xi_m,\xi_{m+1})$, the active functions $B_{m-p,p,\xi},\ldots,B_{m,p,\xi}$ form a basis of $\mathcal P_p$ and sum to one. Globally, the $n$ B-splines form a basis of $S_{p,\xi}$. In particular, every $q\in\mathcal P_p$ has a unique expansion $q=\sum_{j=1}^n c_jB_{j,p,\xi}$ on $[a,b]$.

For one admissible patch map $F:\widehat\Omega\to\Omega$, let $S_h$ be a finite tensor-product B-spline space on a knot grid refining the geometry grid, and let $W$ be the positive denominator of the geometry representation. The parametric rational analysis space is
$$\widehat V_h:=\{s/W:s\in S_h\}.$$
Its physical push-forward is $\{\,\widehat v\circ F^{-1}:\widehat v\in\widehat V_h\,\}$. The homogeneous-Dirichlet conforming space is the subspace of these functions that belongs to $H^1_0(\Omega)$; the unconstrained conforming version is the subspace belonging to $H^1(\Omega)$. These spaces are finite dimensional because the tensor B-spline coefficient set is finite.

For vector-valued elasticity in $\mathbb R^d$, use the componentwise product $\widehat V_h^{\,d}:=(\widehat V_h)^d$, push it forward component by component, and intersect with $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ or $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ as appropriate. This remains finite dimensional because it is a subspace of the finite product of scalar coefficient spaces. Trace equality is required componentwise on each shared full face.

For finitely many matching patches, use one such local rational space on each patch. A global trial function is a piecewise physical function whose traces agree pointwise on every shared full face and which belongs to the chosen global $H^1$ or $H^1_0$ space. Under [[def-countable-choice|Countable Choice]], the vector-valued trace-matching lemma [[lem-matching-nurbs-patch-traces-give-h1-conformity]] proves the H1 part of this interface rule componentwise, including the Cartesian product used for elasticity. Nonmatching interfaces are excluded; a mortar or Nitsche method requires a separate stability and consistency result.

The refinement labels have the following meanings.

- **h-refinement** inserts a new knot into a nonempty span at fixed degree and updates homogeneous control data by [[alg-single-new-b-spline-knot-insertion]]. Theorem [[thm-homogeneous-nurbs-knot-insertion-preserves-patch-geometry]] proves exact map preservation for this operation.
- **p-refinement** raises a coordinate degree and replaces the homogeneous representation only when an exact representation with positive new weights is supplied. A degree label alone does not certify geometry preservation or an approximation rate.
- **k-refinement** raises degree and chooses knot multiplicities to obtain a declared continuity, commonly the maximal $C^{p_r-1}$ continuity at simple interior knots. Exact geometry preservation requires the same positive homogeneous representation check as p-refinement.

On each cell, the pullback of scalar gradients and of the linear-elasticity strain is computed using [[lem-isogeometric-pullback-energy-norm-equivalence]]. Exact geometry does not assert exact quadrature. A discretization using an approximate map or quadrature must retain its separate form and load defects.

Assume Countable Choice. Let a bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, be the union of finitely many bounded knot-cell images with disjoint interiors and a face-to-face finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation. Let $m\ge1$ and let $v: \Omega\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^1$ on the closure of each cell, with each component's cell gradient square integrable. Suppose the two one-sided vector values agree on every shared face. Then $v\in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$; its weak gradient is the piecewise classical componentwise gradient. This is the interface condition used to form conforming multipatch isogeometric spaces. Boundary conditions remain an additional restriction such as membership in $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, bounded, connected, and Lipschitz. Use the real spaces $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ and $Q=L^2_0(D)$, norms $\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(D)}$ and $\|q\|_Q=\|q\|_{L^2(D)}$, and $b(v,q)=-\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}v$ as in [[def-na-stokes-zero-mean-pressure-and-velocity-spaces]]. For a real normed space $X$, write $X'$ for its continuous real dual with operator norm $\|F\|_{X'}=\sup_{\|x\|_X\le1}|F(x)|$. Let $\mu\in L^\infty(D;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $0<\mu_0\le\mu(x)\le\mu_1<\infty$ almost everywhere, let $\lambda\ge0$ be a scalar, and let $f\in V'$. For any $w,z\in H^1(D;\mathbb R^d)$ define $\varepsilon(w)=(\nabla w+\nabla w^T)/2$ and
$$a_\mu(w,z)=2\int_D\mu\,\varepsilon(w):\varepsilon(z),\qquad \mathcal E_\lambda(w,z)=a_\mu(w,z)+\lambda\int_D\operatorname{div}w\,\operatorname{div}z,$$
and $\sigma_\lambda(w)=2\mu\varepsilon(w)+\lambda(\operatorname{div}w)I_d$. The homogeneous-Dirichlet model restricts these forms to $V$, with displacement zero on the full boundary; an example may prescribe a different boundary partition but gains no well-posedness claim from this definition. This is a linear small-strain model; no nonlinear, injectivity, or contrast-independent estimate is asserted.

Countable Choice is inherited through the imported Sobolev and Stokes-space conventions; this definition makes no arbitrary-index selection.

Assume Countable Choice and the data of [[def-linear-elasticity-displacement-formulation-and-data]]. For every finite $\lambda\ge0$ there is a unique $u\in V$ such that $\mathcal E_\lambda(u,v)=f(v)$ for every $v\in V$. It satisfies
$$
\|u\|_V\le\mu_0^{-1}\|f\|_{V'},\qquad \sqrt{\mathcal E_\lambda(u,u)}\le\mu_0^{-1/2}\|f\|_{V'}.
$$
For every finite-dimensional conforming subspace $V_h\subset V$, the Galerkin solution $u_h$ is unique and
$$
\|u-u_h\|_V\le\frac{2\mu_1+d\lambda}{\mu_0}\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_V.
$$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

$a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ be linear in its first argument, conjugate-linear
in its second, bounded by $M$, and coercive with constant $\alpha>0$:
$$|a(v,w)|\le M\|v\|_V\|w\|_V,\qquad \operatorname{Re}a(v,v)\ge\alpha\|v\|_V^2.$$
Let $F:V\to\mathbb K$ be bounded and conjugate-linear, and let $V_h\subseteq V$
be finite-dimensional. Then there are unique $u\in V$ and $u_h\in V_h$ with
$$a(u,v)=F(v)\quad(v\in V).$$
$$a(u_h,v_h)=F(v_h)\quad(v_h\in V_h).$$

$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\frac M\alpha\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_V.$$

For a multi-index $\alpha=(i_1,\ldots,i_d)$ in the finite product index set $\mathcal I$, define the tensor-product basis function
$$N_\alpha(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d):=\prod_{r=1}^d B^{(r)}_{i_r,p_r,\Xi_r}(\xi_r).$$

$$F(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}R_\alpha(\xi)P_\alpha.$$

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$, with the Euclidean

   $$\langle x,y\rangle \;=\; \tfrac14\Bigl(\lVert x+y\rVert_2^{2} - \lVert x-y\rVert_2^{2}\Bigr),$$

there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if

Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that

For one admissible patch map $F:\widehat\Omega\to\Omega$, let $S_h$ be a finite tensor-product B-spline space on a knot grid refining the geometry grid, and let $W$ be the positive denominator of the geometry representation. The parametric rational analysis space is
$$\widehat V_h:=\{s/W:s\in S_h\}.$$
Its physical push-forward is $\{\,\widehat v\circ F^{-1}:\widehat v\in\widehat V_h\,\}$. The homogeneous-Dirichlet conforming space is the subspace of these functions that belongs to $H^1_0(\Omega)$; the unconstrained conforming version is the subspace belonging to $H^1(\Omega)$. For vector-valued elasticity in $\mathbb R^d$, use the componentwise product $\widehat V_h^{\,d}:=(\widehat V_h)^d$, push it forward component by component, and intersect with $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ or $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ as appropriate. For finitely many matching patches, use one such local rational space on each patch. In particular, if $G_N:=\max_\alpha\|\nabla N_\alpha\|_{L^\infty(\text{cells})}$ and $G_W:=w_+\sum_\alpha\|\nabla N_\alpha\|_{L^\infty(\text{cells})}$, then

The inverse pullback also preserves $H^1$, and

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, $a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ a bounded coercive form with boundedness constant $M$ and coercivity constant $\alpha>0$, and $F:V\to\mathbb K$ a bounded functional linear in the real case and conjugate-linear in the complex test argument. Let $V_h\subseteq V$ be finite-dimensional, and let $a_h:V_h\times V_h\to\mathbb K$ and $F_h:V_h\to\mathbb K$ be bounded, with $F_h$ having the same test-linearity as $F$, and $a_h$ coercive with constant $\alpha_h>0$ in the inherited norm. Both $a$ and $a_h$ are sesquilinear (bilinear over $\mathbb R$), linear in their first argument and conjugate-linear in their second over $\mathbb C$. There are unique exact and discrete solutions $u$ and $u_h$, and

$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\left((1+M/\alpha_h)\|u-v_h\|_V+\frac{\delta_{a,h}(v_h)+\delta_{F,h}}{\alpha_h}\right),$$

where the defects are those of [[def-variational-crime-error-framework]]. For a family of meshes this is a uniform estimate whenever $\inf_h\alpha_h>0$ and the displayed approximation and defect terms are uniformly controlled. The term $\delta_{F,h}$ retains source approximation and data oscillation.

Assume Countable Choice and the admissible piecewise $C^1$ NURBS map $F:\widehat\Omega\to\Omega$ of [[def-nurbs-patch-map-and-rational-spline-space]]. Write $J_F=\det DF$, and assume $j_-\le J_F\le j_+$ and $\|DF\|_{\mathrm{op}},\|DF^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L$ almost everywhere on the cells. For every $u\in H^1(\Omega)$, its pullback $\widehat u=u\circ F$ lies in $H^1(\widehat\Omega)$, with cellwise weak gradient
$$\nabla_\xi\widehat u=DF^\mathsf T(\nabla_xu)\circ F.$$
The inverse pullback also preserves $H^1$, and
$$\|\widehat u\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)}\le j_-^{-1/2}\sqrt{1+L^2}\,\|u\|_{H^1(\Omega)},\qquad \|u\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le j_+^{1/2}\sqrt{1+L^2}\,\|\widehat u\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)}.$$
Pullback maps $H^1_0(\Omega)$ onto $H^1_0(\widehat\Omega)$. For a vector field $\widehat v=v\circ F$, the physical gradient is $(\nabla_\xi\widehat v)DF^{-1}$, so the scalar diffusion and finite-Lamé elasticity forms are transformed by the same Jacobian and inverse-map factors.

Let $d\in\{2,3\}$, let $F,G:(0,1)^d\to\mathbb R^d$ be admissible piecewise $C^1$ maps on a common finite refinement of their knot partitions, and suppose almost everywhere that both maps have positive Jacobian determinants and
$$\|DF\|_{\rm op},\|DG\|_{\rm op},\|DF^{-1}\|_{\rm op},\|DG^{-1}\|_{\rm op}\le M,\qquad M\ge1.$$
Set $\delta=\|DF-DG\|_{L^\infty({\rm op})}$, the essential supremum of the operator-norm difference on that common refinement, and define the unit-diffusion pullback tensors
$$K_F=(\det DF)DF^{-1}DF^{-\mathsf T},\qquad K_G=(\det DG)DG^{-1}DG^{-\mathsf T}.$$
Then, almost everywhere,
$$\|K_F-K_G\|_{\rm op}\le(dM^{d+1}+2M^{d+3})\delta.$$
Consequently, for $v,w\in H^1((0,1)^d)$,
$$\left|\int_{(0,1)^d}(K_F-K_G)\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\right|\le(dM^{d+1}+2M^{d+3})\delta\,\|\nabla v\|_2\|\nabla w\|_2.$$
The discrepancy is a derivative-map error; a bound on $\|F-G\|_\infty$ alone is not used.

Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. In the **exact variational problem**, $V$ is a Hilbert space, $a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ is a bounded coercive sesquilinear form (bilinear when $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$), linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second when $\mathbb K=\mathbb C$, and $F:V\to\mathbb K$ is bounded and has the same linearity in its test argument as the second argument of $a$. Exact solutions satisfy $a(u,v)=F(v)$ for every $v\in V$. Boundedness and coercivity have the meanings in [[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]].

For a **conforming perturbed Galerkin problem**, $V_h\subseteq V$ is a finite-dimensional subspace, $a_h:V_h\times V_h\to\mathbb K$ and $F_h:V_h\to\mathbb K$ are the discrete form and load, and $u_h\in V_h$ solves $a_h(u_h,w_h)=F_h(w_h)$. Its discrete coercivity constant is any $\alpha_h>0$ such that $\operatorname{Re}a_h(w_h,w_h)\ge\alpha_h\|w_h\|_V^2$ for every $w_h\in V_h$. For $v_h\in V_h$, define

$$\delta_{a,h}(v_h):=\sup_{w_h\in V_h\setminus\{0\}}\frac{|a(v_h,w_h)-a_h(v_h,w_h)|}{\|w_h\|_V},\qquad \delta_{F,h}:=\sup_{w_h\in V_h\setminus\{0\}}\frac{|F(w_h)-F_h(w_h)|}{\|w_h\|_V}.$$

If $V_h=\{0\}$, both defects are defined to be zero. The load defect $\delta_{F,h}$ includes any source approximation or data oscillation; it is not assumed small or zero without a separate bound.

For a **nonconforming problem**, the exact space $V$ and finite-dimensional trial space $V_h$ need not satisfy $V_h\subseteq V$. Put $X_h:=V+V_h$ and equip it with a norm $\|\cdot\|_h$ whose restrictions to $V$ and $V_h$ are norms. The discrete form $a_h$ is defined on $V_h\times V_h$, and a bounded extension $\widetilde a_h:X_h\times V_h\to\mathbb K$ means $\widetilde a_h=a_h$ on $V_h\times V_h$ and $|\widetilde a_h(z,w_h)|\le M_h\|z\|_h\|w_h\|_h$. For an exact solution $u\in V$, define the nonconforming consistency defect

$$\delta^{\mathrm{nc}}_h(u):=\sup_{w_h\in V_h\setminus\{0\}}\frac{|F_h(w_h)-\widetilde a_h(u,w_h)|}{\|w_h\|_h},$$

with value zero if $V_h=\{0\}$. This residual need not vanish: the exact weak equation is only asserted for tests in $V$.

Geometry and quadrature defects are components of the appropriate form defect when the implemented form is compared with the pulled-back exact form. No exact Galerkin orthogonality is asserted after replacing the form or test space.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, $a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ a bounded coercive form with boundedness constant $M$ and coercivity constant $\alpha>0$, and $F:V\to\mathbb K$ a bounded functional linear in the real case and conjugate-linear in the complex test argument. Let $V_h\subseteq V$ be finite-dimensional, and let $a_h:V_h\times V_h\to\mathbb K$ and $F_h:V_h\to\mathbb K$ be bounded, with $F_h$ having the same test-linearity as $F$, and $a_h$ coercive with constant $\alpha_h>0$ in the inherited norm. Both $a$ and $a_h$ are sesquilinear (bilinear over $\mathbb R$), linear in their first argument and conjugate-linear in their second over $\mathbb C$. There are unique exact and discrete solutions $u$ and $u_h$, and

$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\left((1+M/\alpha_h)\|u-v_h\|_V+\frac{\delta_{a,h}(v_h)+\delta_{F,h}}{\alpha_h}\right),$$

where the defects are those of [[def-variational-crime-error-framework]]. For a family of meshes this is a uniform estimate whenever $\inf_h\alpha_h>0$ and the displayed approximation and defect terms are uniformly controlled. The term $\delta_{F,h}$ retains source approximation and data oscillation.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F,G$ be two admissible tensor-product NURBS maps on $\overline Q=[0,1]^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, with finite knot partitions. Geometry continuity is required even if a representation allows a degree-plus-one interior knot; in particular it follows from degrees $p_r\ge1$ and interior multiplicities $\mu_r\le p_r$. Take the union of all distinct knots in each coordinate, discard zero-length spans, and let $\mathcal C$ be the resulting common rectangular partition. On each closed $C\in\mathcal C$, use the polynomial expressions inherited from the incident open cell, rather than a discontinuous evaluation convention at an endpoint. Their positive denominators, positive Jacobian lower bounds and bounded map/inverse derivatives are required on these expressions. They follow by continuity from uniform cellwise admissibility bounds. No agreement of cross-face normal derivatives is required.

For $C=a+\operatorname{diag}(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_d)[0,1]^d$, subdivide by the $d!$ simplices
$$T_{C,\pi}=\{a+\operatorname{diag}(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_d)t:0\le t_{\pi(1)}\le\cdots\le t_{\pi(d)}\le1\},\qquad \pi\in\mathfrak S_d.$$
These form a matching affine simplicial mesh of $\overline Q$. The restricted maps $F|_{T_{C,\pi}}$ and $G|_{T_{C,\pi}}$ are admissible curved-cell maps in [[def-isoparametric-curved-cell-map]], with the reference simplices taken in parameter coordinates. Their images are matching curved partitions, and the two global maps satisfy [[def-curved-domain-geometry-approximation]] with $\Phi=F$, $\Phi_h=G$, $\Omega=F(Q)$ and $\Omega_h=G(Q)$. The geometry errors are precisely $e_0=\|F-G\|_\infty$ and $e_1=\|DF-DG\|_{L^\infty(\text{cells};op)}$ on the box; subdivision does not change their essential suprema. Matching traces means agreement within each mapped mesh across shared facets, not $F=G$ on the exterior boundary. A prescribed common exterior boundary requires a separate equality of those traces. Common image topology is given by the homeomorphism $G\circ F^{-1}$.

For each finite cell, the rational expression has a smooth extension to a neighborhood of its closed rectangle: its polynomial numerator and denominator extend there and the denominator remains positive after shrinking the neighborhood. Its second derivatives are therefore bounded on that closed cell. For a sequence of grids, uniform reference-simplex shape regularity follows if $\max_r\ell_r/\min_r\ell_r\le\kappa$ on every rectangle with fixed $\kappa$. Uniform curved-map bounds additionally require uniform first, inverse and second derivative bounds of the rational cell expressions. Neither uniform second derivative bounds nor a shape constant follows from a first derivative error bound alone. The construction changes the geometry presentation only; rational analysis functions remain rational and are not reclassified as affine P1 functions.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $Q=(0,1)^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$. Use a common finite tensor-product B-spline basis $N_\alpha$ of coordinate degrees $p_r\ge1$, clamped endpoint multiplicities $p_r+1$, and interior multiplicities at most $p_r$. Only positive-length knot spans are cells. Exact homogeneous re-representation on this common basis must be established before comparing data on originally different grids; it is not inferred from a common geometric image. Let
$$A=\sum_\alpha a_\alpha N_\alpha,\quad W=\sum_\alpha w_\alpha N_\alpha,\quad F=A/W,\qquad A'=\sum_\alpha a'_\alpha N_\alpha,\quad W'=\sum_\alpha w'_\alpha N_\alpha,\quad G=A'/W'.$$
Here $a_\alpha=w_\alpha P_\alpha\in\mathbb R^d$ and $a'_\alpha=w'_\alpha P'_\alpha$. Suppose $F$ is admissible in [[def-nurbs-patch-map-and-rational-spline-space]], $w_-\le w_\alpha\le w_+$, $\|DF\|,\|(DF)^{-1}\|\le L$, $\det DF\ge j_->0$, and the global lower Lipschitz bound is explicitly $|F(x)-F(y)|\ge c|x-y|$ on $\overline Q$, $c>0$. The latter is the reciprocal of a global inverse Lipschitz bound and need not equal $1/L$.

Define finite data quantities
$$\epsilon_A=\max_\alpha|a'_\alpha-a_\alpha|,\quad \epsilon_W=\max_\alpha|w'_\alpha-w_\alpha|<w_-,\quad m=w_--\epsilon_W>0,\quad R=\max_\alpha|P_\alpha|,$$
$$H=\sum_\alpha\max_C\|\nabla N_\alpha\|_{L^\infty(C)},\quad T=\epsilon_A+R\epsilon_W,\qquad E_0=T/m,$$
$$E_1=\frac{H\epsilon_A+L\epsilon_W+RH\epsilon_W}{m}+\frac{T(w_++\epsilon_W)H}{m^2}.$$
All vector norms are Euclidean and all derivative norms are operator norms. $H$ is defined by the actual cell polynomials, so retains every degree, knot-spacing and multiplicity dependence. It is finite on each fixed finite nondegenerate grid; no uniform bound over degenerating grids is asserted. Then $w'_\alpha\ge m$, $G$ is continuous on $\overline Q$, and
$$e_0:=\|F-G\|_\infty\le E_0,\qquad e_1:=\|DF-DG\|_{L^\infty(\text{cells};op)}\le E_1.$$
If $E_1<\min(c,1/L)$, then $G$ is globally injective and bi-Lipschitz onto its image, and
$$|G(x)-G(y)|\ge(c-E_1)|x-y|,\quad \|DG\|\le L+E_1,\quad \|(DG)^{-1}\|\le\frac{L}{1-LE_1},\quad \det DG\ge j_-(1-LE_1)^d>0.$$
The image $G(Q)$ is open. For the admissible-patch conclusion, retain the explicit boundary hypothesis that $G(Q)$ is a Lipschitz domain with its finite piecewise $C^1$ knot-cell presentation. A sufficient verifiable alternative is that $G$ extends $C^1$ to a neighborhood of $\overline Q$ with nonsingular derivative there; this alternative holds when every interior multiplicity is at most $p_r-1$. With either boundary condition $G$ is admissible. No equality of the physical boundaries of $F(Q)$ and $G(Q)$ is asserted; their correspondence is $G\circ F^{-1}$.

For these admissible maps put
$$M=\max\left(1,L,L+E_1,\frac{L}{1-LE_1}\right),\qquad C_M=dM^{d+1}+2M^{d+3}.$$
Their unit-Laplace tensors satisfy $\|K_F-K_G\|_\infty\le C_ME_1$, and their bilinear-form difference is at most $C_ME_1\|\nabla v\|_2\|\nabla w\|_2$. For any family with uniformly bounded $L,c^{-1},R,w_+,m^{-1}$ and $H\epsilon_A+H\epsilon_W+\epsilon_W=O(h^s)$, $s>0$, the geometry form defect is $O(h^s)$. The bound is generated from homogeneous data; convergence of those data remains a separate approximation or certification obligation. Loads, quadrature and boundary-lift defects remain separate.

A concrete geometry generator is scalar rounding of every component of $a_\alpha$ and every $w_\alpha$ to the nearest multiple of $2^{-b}$ (ties go to the smaller integer), followed by $P'_\alpha=a'_\alpha/w'_\alpha$. Put $\eta_b=2^{-b-1}$ and
$$D=\frac{2H\sqrt d+2L+2RH}{w_-}+\frac{4(\sqrt d+R)(w_++w_-/2)H}{w_-^2}.$$
Choose an integer $b\ge0$ such that $\eta_b<\min(w_-/2,c/(2D),1/(2LD))$. Then this generator has $\epsilon_A\le\sqrt d\,\eta_b$, $\epsilon_W\le\eta_b$, $e_0\le2(\sqrt d+R)\eta_b/w_-$, and $e_1\le D\eta_b$; in particular it generates the positive denominator, Jacobian, and global injectivity bounds above. In the $C^1$ knot branch ($\mu_r\le p_r-1$) it generates admissible approximate domains without an independent boundary certificate. Taking $b$ so that $D\eta_b\le h^s$ produces a stated geometry derivative rate for any supplied grid family, with its actual $D$, rather than claiming a rate from positive weights or knot refinement alone.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. On $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]) define $$(u,v)_{H^1}:=(u,v)_{L^2}+\sum_{i=1}^n(D_iu,D_iv)_{L^2},$$ with the $L^2$ inner product of [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. Then $(\cdot,\cdot)_{H^1}$ is an inner product on the Sobolev classes whose induced norm is the $W^{1,2}$ norm of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and $H^1(\Omega)$ is a Hilbert space for it. The zero-boundary space $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a closed subspace of $H^1(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]) and hence a Hilbert space for the restricted inner product. The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, in the convention of [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]].

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, and suppose its first coordinate projection is contained in an interval $(a,b)$ of width $L=b-a$. For every real $v\in H^1_0(D)$,

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let the unit cube be partitioned into uniform tensor cells of side length $h=1/N$. Let $g\in C^1([0,1]^d)$ have Lipschitz gradient with constant $M_g$, meaning $|\nabla g(x)-\nabla g(y)|\le M_g|x-y|$ for all $x,y$. Let $I_hg$ be the continuous tensor-product, degree-one nodal interpolant matching $g$ at every grid vertex. Then $I_hg$ lies in the tensor-product degree-one $C^0$ spline space and
$$\|g-I_hg\|_{H^1((0,1)^d)}\le C_d h M_g,\qquad C_d:=d+\sqrt d+2^{d-1}d\sqrt d.$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be open and let $z\in H^1(U)$ vanish almost everywhere outside a compact set $K\subset U$. Then $z\in H^1_0(U)$, where $H^1_0(U)$ is the $H^1$ closure of $C_c^\infty(U)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let a bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, be the union of finitely many bounded knot-cell images with disjoint interiors and a face-to-face finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation. Let $m\ge1$ and let $v: \Omega\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^1$ on the closure of each cell, with each component's cell gradient square integrable. Suppose the two one-sided vector values agree on every shared face. Then $v\in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$; its weak gradient is the piecewise classical componentwise gradient. This is the interface condition used to form conforming multipatch isogeometric spaces. Boundary conditions remain an additional restriction such as membership in $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F:\widehat\Omega\to\Omega$ be an admissible NURBS map and $W$ its continuous denominator, with $W\ge w_->0$ and cellwise $G_W:=\|\nabla W\|_{L^\infty}<\infty$. Let $\widehat u$ be real-valued and let $s\in S_h$ be a real numerator spline; assume both are $C^1$ up to the boundary of each cell in the common refinement of the geometry and analysis knot grids, with matching traces, and put $g:=W\widehat u$. Then the physical rational spline $v_h:=(s/W)\circ F^{-1}$ belongs to $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and
$$\|u-v_h\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C_F C_W\|g-s\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)},\qquad C_F:=\sqrt{j_+}\sqrt{1+L^2},\quad C_W:=\frac{2}{w_-}+\frac{G_W}{w_-^2},$$
where $u:=\widehat u\circ F^{-1}$. This result transfers a specified numerator approximation bound; it does not assert a polynomial-degree-independent rate or a general $H^1$ rate for arbitrary knot families.

Assume Countable Choice and the admissible piecewise $C^1$ NURBS map $F:\widehat\Omega\to\Omega$ of [[def-nurbs-patch-map-and-rational-spline-space]]. Write $J_F=\det DF$, and assume $j_-\le J_F\le j_+$ and $\|DF\|_{\mathrm{op}},\|DF^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L$ almost everywhere on the cells. For every $u\in H^1(\Omega)$, its pullback $\widehat u=u\circ F$ lies in $H^1(\widehat\Omega)$, with cellwise weak gradient
$$\nabla_\xi\widehat u=DF^\mathsf T(\nabla_xu)\circ F.$$
The inverse pullback also preserves $H^1$, and
$$\|\widehat u\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)}\le j_-^{-1/2}\sqrt{1+L^2}\,\|u\|_{H^1(\Omega)},\qquad \|u\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le j_+^{1/2}\sqrt{1+L^2}\,\|\widehat u\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)}.$$
Pullback maps $H^1_0(\Omega)$ onto $H^1_0(\widehat\Omega)$. For a vector field $\widehat v=v\circ F$, the physical gradient is $(\nabla_\xi\widehat v)DF^{-1}$, so the scalar diffusion and finite-Lamé elasticity forms are transformed by the same Jacobian and inverse-map factors.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, be bounded, connected, and Lipschitz, and let $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R)$ with norm $\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(D)}$. Let $A:D\to\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ be measurable and symmetric, with constants $0<\alpha\le\beta<\infty$ such that
$$\zeta\cdot A(x)\zeta\ge\alpha|\zeta|^2\quad\text{and}\quad\|A(x)\|_{\rm op}\le\beta\quad\text{for a.e. }x\in D,\ \zeta\in\mathbb R^d.$$
For $f\in V'$, define $a(u,v)=\int_D A\nabla u\cdot\nabla v$ and $F(v)=f(v)$. Let $V_h\subset V$ be any finite conforming isogeometric subspace on the exact admissible patch geometry. Then the weak problem and its Galerkin restriction have unique solutions $u$ and $u_h$, and
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_V.$$
This is an exact-form estimate; it makes no assertion about approximate geometry, quadrature, polynomial-degree-independent constants, or a rate without a separate numerator approximation theorem.

derivations.claim: If $g=0$, then $s=0$, $u=v_h=0$ and the result is immediate. Otherwise use the nonempty support set $K$ from the Statement. Every tensor cell meeting $\partial\widehat\Omega$ has all its vertices outside $K$: each vertex is within $\sqrt d\,h$ of a boundary point. Therefore $g$ is zero at those vertices, and the cellwise Q1 interpolant is identically zero on each such boundary cell. The function $s:=I_hg$ is continuous, has support in the compact $\sqrt d h$-neighborhood of $K$ inside $\widehat\Omega$, and is a degree-one tensor spline by [F1]. Both $s/W$ and $g/W$ are piecewise $C^1$, have matching traces because $s,g,W$ are continuous and $W\ge w_->0$, and have square-integrable cell gradients. By [F3] they belong to $H^1$; their supports are compact in the reference box, so [F2] puts them in $H^1_0(\widehat\Omega)$. Pullback by [F5] gives $v_h,u\in H^1_0(D)$.

The grid compatibility in the Statement makes $s=I_hg$ an element of the numerator space defining $V_h$. Apply [F4] with target numerator $g=W\widehat u$ and approximating numerator $s$. The numerator $g$ is C1 on the closed box, $s$ is a continuous cellwise polynomial, and the continuous denominator $W$ is a positive cellwise polynomial. Hence $g/W$ and $s/W$ are C1 up to each common-refinement cell boundary and have matching traces; Countable Choice is [A1], so all hypotheses hold and $\|u-v_h\|_{H^1(D)}\le C_FC_W\|g-I_hg\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)}\le C_FC_WC_dhM_g,$ where the final inequality is [F1].

Apply the exact-form Galerkin estimate [F6] and use $v_h$ as a candidate in its best-approximation infimum. The gradient error is at most $(\beta/\alpha)\|u-v_h\|_{H^1(D)}$; insert step 1.2 to obtain the displayed bound. No quadrature, perturbed geometry, or high-degree approximation rate is used.

Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let the reference patch be $\widehat\Omega=(0,1)^d$. For each coordinate $r$, fix a degree $p_r\in\mathbb N_0$, a finite clamped knot vector $\Xi_r$ on $[0,1]$, and its one-dimensional B-spline basis $B^{(r)}_{i_r,p_r,\Xi_r}$ from [[def-b-spline-space-and-basis]]. For a multi-index $\alpha=(i_1,\ldots,i_d)$ in the finite product index set $\mathcal I$, define the tensor-product basis function
$$N_\alpha(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d):=\prod_{r=1}^d B^{(r)}_{i_r,p_r,\Xi_r}(\xi_r).$$

Choose finitely many control points $P_\alpha\in\mathbb R^d$ and positive weights $w_\alpha$, and write $0<w_-:=\min_\alpha w_\alpha\le\max_\alpha w_\alpha=:w_+<\infty$. The weight denominator, rational basis, and associated rational spline space are
$$W(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}w_\alpha N_\alpha(\xi),\qquad R_\alpha(\xi):=\frac{w_\alpha N_\alpha(\xi)}{W(\xi)},\qquad \mathcal N_h:=\operatorname{span}\{R_\alpha:\alpha\in\mathcal I\}.$$
The corresponding NURBS geometry map is
$$F(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}R_\alpha(\xi)P_\alpha.$$
Equivalently, let $\widetilde F(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}(w_\alpha P_\alpha,w_\alpha)N_\alpha(\xi)\in\mathbb R^{d+1}$ and let $\Pi(y,z):=y/z$ for $z>0$. Then $F=\Pi\circ\widetilde F$ wherever $W>0$.
The basis properties in [[thm-spline-polynomial-reproduction]] give nonnegative tensor factors summing to one. Consequently the weights' convex combination satisfies $W\ge w_->0$; the later item `lem-positive-nurbs-basis-and-quotient-derivative` records the full rational-basis consequences.

An admissible NURBS patch map is a continuous, globally injective, bi-Lipschitz map $F:\overline{\widehat\Omega}\to\overline\Omega$ whose restriction to every nonempty knot cell is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism onto its image. There are constants $0<j_-\le j_+<\infty$ and $1\le L<\infty$ such that, almost everywhere on every cell,
$$j_-\le J_F:=\det DF\le j_+,\qquad \|DF\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L,\qquad \|DF^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L.$$
The physical image $\Omega$ is required to be a bounded Lipschitz domain. The images of the finite knot cells form a face-to-face partition with the piecewise $C^1$ boundary presentation of [[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]]; the map agrees on each shared cell face.

A finite multipatch geometry consists of finitely many such patch maps with disjoint physical interiors, a connected bounded Lipschitz union, and matching full physical faces wherever two patches meet. Positive weights only define a positive denominator and a convex rational basis; they do not assert global injectivity, positive Jacobian, or interface matching. Exact NURBS representation means exact representation of the specified CAD map and does not assert that this map is the exact geometry of a target physical domain.

For the finite tensor-product basis and weights of [[def-nurbs-patch-map-and-rational-spline-space]], the denominator satisfies $w_-\le W(\xi)\le w_+$, the rational basis is nonnegative and sums to one, and
$$\mathcal N_h=\{s/W:s\in S_h\},\qquad S_h:=\operatorname{span}\{N_\alpha:\alpha\in\mathcal I\}.$$
On each open knot cell, the rational basis functions are differentiable and
$$\nabla R_\alpha=\frac{w_\alpha}{W}\nabla N_\alpha-\frac{w_\alpha N_\alpha}{W^2}\nabla W.$$
In particular, if $G_N:=\max_\alpha\|\nabla N_\alpha\|_{L^\infty(\text{cells})}$ and $G_W:=w_+\sum_\alpha\|\nabla N_\alpha\|_{L^\infty(\text{cells})}$, then
$$\|\nabla R_\alpha\|_{L^\infty(\text{cells})}\le \frac{w_+G_N}{w_-}+\frac{w_+G_W}{w_-^2}.$$
These derivative bounds depend on the fixed degrees and knot cells; no degree-independent bound is asserted.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, let

$\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n$ be the multi-index of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]. We say that $v$ is
the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$

$$\widehat V_h:=\{s/W:s\in S_h\}.$$
Its physical push-forward is $\{\,\widehat v\circ F^{-1}:\widehat v\in\widehat V_h\,\}$. The homogeneous-Dirichlet conforming space is the subspace of these functions that belongs to $H^1_0(\Omega)$; the unconstrained conforming version is the subspace belonging to $H^1(\Omega)$. These spaces are finite dimensional because the tensor B-spline coefficient set is finite.

For vector-valued elasticity in $\mathbb R^d$, use the componentwise product $\widehat V_h^{\,d}:=(\widehat V_h)^d$, push it forward component by component, and intersect with $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ or $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ as appropriate. This remains finite dimensional because it is a subspace of the finite product of scalar coefficient spaces. Trace equality is required componentwise on each shared full face.

For finitely many matching patches, use one such local rational space on each patch. A global trial function is a piecewise physical function whose traces agree pointwise on every shared full face and which belongs to the chosen global $H^1$ or $H^1_0$ space. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let the reference patch be $\widehat\Omega=(0,1)^d$. For each coordinate $r$, fix a degree $p_r\in\mathbb N_0$, a finite clamped knot vector $\Xi_r$ on $[0,1]$, and its one-dimensional B-spline basis $B^{(r)}_{i_r,p_r,\Xi_r}$ from [[def-b-spline-space-and-basis]]. For a multi-index $\alpha=(i_1,\ldots,i_d)$ in the finite product index set $\mathcal I$, define the tensor-product basis function
$$N_\alpha(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d):=\prod_{r=1}^d B^{(r)}_{i_r,p_r,\Xi_r}(\xi_r).$$

Choose finitely many control points $P_\alpha\in\mathbb R^d$ and positive weights $w_\alpha$, and write $0<w_-:=\min_\alpha w_\alpha\le\max_\alpha w_\alpha=:w_+<\infty$. The weight denominator, rational basis, and associated rational spline space are
$$W(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}w_\alpha N_\alpha(\xi),\qquad R_\alpha(\xi):=\frac{w_\alpha N_\alpha(\xi)}{W(\xi)},\qquad \mathcal N_h:=\operatorname{span}\{R_\alpha:\alpha\in\mathcal I\}.$$
The corresponding NURBS geometry map is
$$F(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}R_\alpha(\xi)P_\alpha.$$
Equivalently, let $\widetilde F(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}(w_\alpha P_\alpha,w_\alpha)N_\alpha(\xi)\in\mathbb R^{d+1}$ and let $\Pi(y,z):=y/z$ for $z>0$. Then $F=\Pi\circ\widetilde F$ wherever $W>0$.
The basis properties in [[thm-spline-polynomial-reproduction]] give nonnegative tensor factors summing to one. Consequently the weights' convex combination satisfies $W\ge w_->0$; the later item `lem-positive-nurbs-basis-and-quotient-derivative` records the full rational-basis consequences.

An admissible NURBS patch map is a continuous, globally injective, bi-Lipschitz map $F:\overline{\widehat\Omega}\to\overline\Omega$ whose restriction to every nonempty knot cell is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism onto its image. There are constants $0<j_-\le j_+<\infty$ and $1\le L<\infty$ such that, almost everywhere on every cell,
$$j_-\le J_F:=\det DF\le j_+,\qquad \|DF\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L,\qquad \|DF^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L.$$
The physical image $\Omega$ is required to be a bounded Lipschitz domain. The images of the finite knot cells form a face-to-face partition with the piecewise $C^1$ boundary presentation of [[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]]; the map agrees on each shared cell face.

A finite multipatch geometry consists of finitely many such patch maps with disjoint physical interiors, a connected bounded Lipschitz union, and matching full physical faces wherever two patches meet. Positive weights only define a positive denominator and a convex rational basis; they do not assert global injectivity, positive Jacobian, or interface matching. Exact NURBS representation means exact representation of the specified CAD map and does not assert that this map is the exact geometry of a target physical domain.

For the finite tensor-product basis and weights of [[def-nurbs-patch-map-and-rational-spline-space]], the denominator satisfies $w_-\le W(\xi)\le w_+$, the rational basis is nonnegative and sums to one, and
$$\mathcal N_h=\{s/W:s\in S_h\},\qquad S_h:=\operatorname{span}\{N_\alpha:\alpha\in\mathcal I\}.$$
On each open knot cell, the rational basis functions are differentiable and
$$\nabla R_\alpha=\frac{w_\alpha}{W}\nabla N_\alpha-\frac{w_\alpha N_\alpha}{W^2}\nabla W.$$
In particular, if $G_N:=\max_\alpha\|\nabla N_\alpha\|_{L^\infty(\text{cells})}$ and $G_W:=w_+\sum_\alpha\|\nabla N_\alpha\|_{L^\infty(\text{cells})}$, then
$$\|\nabla R_\alpha\|_{L^\infty(\text{cells})}\le \frac{w_+G_N}{w_-}+\frac{w_+G_W}{w_-^2}.$$
These derivative bounds depend on the fixed degrees and knot cells; no degree-independent bound is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice and the admissible piecewise $C^1$ NURBS map $F:\widehat\Omega\to\Omega$ of [[def-nurbs-patch-map-and-rational-spline-space]]. Write $J_F=\det DF$, and assume $j_-\le J_F\le j_+$ and $\|DF\|_{\mathrm{op}},\|DF^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L$ almost everywhere on the cells. For every $u\in H^1(\Omega)$, its pullback $\widehat u=u\circ F$ lies in $H^1(\widehat\Omega)$, with cellwise weak gradient
$$\nabla_\xi\widehat u=DF^\mathsf T(\nabla_xu)\circ F.$$
The inverse pullback also preserves $H^1$, and
$$\|\widehat u\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)}\le j_-^{-1/2}\sqrt{1+L^2}\,\|u\|_{H^1(\Omega)},\qquad \|u\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le j_+^{1/2}\sqrt{1+L^2}\,\|\widehat u\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)}.$$
Pullback maps $H^1_0(\Omega)$ onto $H^1_0(\widehat\Omega)$. For a vector field $\widehat v=v\circ F$, the physical gradient is $(\nabla_\xi\widehat v)DF^{-1}$, so the scalar diffusion and finite-Lamé elasticity forms are transformed by the same Jacobian and inverse-map factors.

derivations.claim: Put $a=\sqrt2$ and $x_0(t)=(1-t)^2+a t(1-t),\qquad y_0(t)=t^2+a t(1-t),\qquad D(t)=(1-t)^2+a t(1-t)+t^2.$ The weighted middle Bernstein coefficient is $2(1/\sqrt2)t(1-t)=a t(1-t)$, so the angular map is $(X,Y)=(x_0/D,y_0/D)$. Direct expansion gives $x_0^2+y_0^2-D^2=-2t^2(1-t)^2+a^2t^2(1-t)^2=0,$ so $X^2+Y^2=1$; also $X,Y\ge0$ and $D>0$. The tensor-product weights and controls therefore give $F(s,t)=(\rho(s)X(t),\rho(s)Y(t))$.

Expanding the numerator derivatives gives $x_0y_0'-y_0x_0'=a+2(1-a)t(1-t)=aD(t),$ because $D(t)=1+(a-2)t(1-t)$ and $a(a-2)=2(1-a)$. Consequently $XY'-YX'=a/D(t)>0$. Since $X^2+Y^2=1$, the angular coordinate $\theta(t)=\arctan(Y/X)$ has derivative $\theta'=XY'-YX'=a/D(t)>0$ on the interior and extends monotonically from $0$ to $\pi/2$. Thus $t\mapsto(X,Y)$ traverses the first-quadrant unit-circle arc exactly once. Since $\rho$ increases bijectively from $r_0$ to $1$, $F$ is injective and its image is exactly the stated quarter annulus.

The Jacobian is $\det DF(s,t)=\rho'(s)\rho(s)(XY'-YX')=(1-r_0)\rho(s)\frac{\sqrt2}{D(t)}>0.$ On the closed square, $\rho\ge r_0>0$ and $D$ is continuous and positive, so this determinant has positive minimum and finite maximum; $DF$ is continuous and bounded, and the inverse matrix is bounded by its cofactor formula divided by the positive determinant. The physical inverse first recovers $\rho=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ and the angle $\theta=\operatorname{atan2}(y,x)$. This angle is Lipschitz on the annular sector because $\rho\ge r_0$, and the inverse parameter $t(\theta)$ is Lipschitz because $\theta'(t)=\sqrt2/D(t)$ has a positive minimum. Together with the linear inverse for $s$, this makes $F^{-1}$ Lipschitz; bounded $DF$ makes $F$ Lipschitz. The quarter annulus has a finite piecewise smooth Lipschitz boundary, so all admissibility hypotheses in [F1] hold. Applying [F3] gives the announced pullback norm equivalence.

$$j_-\le J_F:=\det DF\le j_+,\qquad \|DF\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L,\qquad \|DF^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L.$$

Fix an integer $d\ge2$. The underlying coordinate index set of $\mathbb R^d$

$1\le i\le d$ are relabeled by $i\mapsto i-1$: write
$\widehat x_i:=\widehat x(i-1)$, and let $e_i\in\mathbb R^d$ be the function
on $I_d$ with $e_i(i-1)=1$ and $e_i(k)=0$ for $k\ne i-1$.
The vertex and barycentric labels $0,\ldots,d$ are distinct from these
underlying coordinate indices. The **reference open simplex** is
$$\widehat S_d:=\{\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d:\widehat x_i>0\ (1\le i\le d),\ \sum_{i=1}^d\widehat x_i<1\},$$

A **matching affine simplicial mesh** of a bounded polyhedral open set

nondegenerate $d$-simplices such that their union is $\overline\Omega$,
their interiors are pairwise disjoint, $\Omega$ is the interior of their
union, and the intersection of two distinct cells is either empty or a
whole face of each. Thus no lower-dimensional crack is omitted from
$\Omega$ while its surrounding cells are retained. Every interior facet is
incident to exactly two cells and every boundary facet to one. The faces of
a cell are the convex hulls of its vertex subsets. A facet means a face of
dimension $d-1$.

For each cell $K\in\mathcal T$, an affine bijection
$$F_K:\overline{\widehat S_d}\to K,\qquad F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x,$$
with invertible $A_K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is a **reference map**.

used for Piola formulas. Write $h_K:=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and let
$\rho_K$ be the radius of the largest Euclidean ball contained in $K$.
A family $\{\mathcal T_h\}_{h\in H}$ is **shape regular** if there is a
finite $\sigma$ such that $h_K/\rho_K\le\sigma$ for every
$h\in H$ and $K\in\mathcal T_h$. This universal condition is vacuous for
an empty family.
This definition uses radius; references using the diameter of the inscribed
ball differ by a factor of two.

An affine image of the reference square is a parallelogram. A general
quadrilateral requires a nonaffine map and is outside this affine definition;
curved-cell approximation is not included here.

countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: In the normalized cube every point has some ordering of its $d$ coordinates, hence belongs to at least one displayed simplex; strict order specifies exactly one interior. For a permutation $\pi$, the closed ordered region is the convex hull of the chain vertices $0,e_{\pi(d)},e_{\pi(d)}+e_{\pi(d-1)},\ldots,\sum_{r=1}^de_{\pi(r)}$: the barycentric coefficients are $1-t_{\pi(d)}$, $t_{\pi(d)}-t_{\pi(d-1)},\ldots,t_{\pi(2)}-t_{\pi(1)},t_{\pi(1)}$. Thus a tie between consecutive coordinates sets exactly the corresponding barycentric coefficient to zero. For two permutations, the common weak order groups precisely the coordinates whose order is reversed into equal blocks; their intersection is the convex hull of the common chain vertices at the block boundaries, hence is a whole face of each simplex. This proves the subdivision is a simplicial complex with disjoint interiors. On a rectangular face one coordinate is $0$ or $1$; the remaining subdivision orders the remaining normalized coordinates. Adjacent rectangles have the same intervals in those coordinates and the same increasing-axis convention, so their induced face subdivisions coincide. The affine diagonal maps preserve these face identities. Therefore the finite subdivision is a matching affine simplicial mesh as required in [F2].

On a closed rectangle each map is a quotient of finite polynomials with denominator bounded below by a positive number. Its cell expression therefore extends smoothly across the rectangle into a neighborhood. Its derivatives, including second derivatives, are bounded there after shrinking the neighborhood. The determinant extends continuously with a positive lower bound on the closed cell. Its restriction to each closed simplex is injective by global injectivity of the map on $\overline Q$. This restriction actually extends injectively to some neighborhood of that simplex: otherwise there exist distinct pairs of points at distance at most $1/n$ from the simplex with equal images. Compactness [F3] gives convergent subsequences with limits in the simplex; equality of images and injectivity force the same limit, contradicting local injectivity [F3] near that limit. A smaller neighborhood retains positive determinant, so the restriction is a neighborhood diffeomorphism. These arguments apply separately to $F$ and $G$.

Continuity of the original maps makes the restricted traces agree on shared simplex facets, including those lying on original knot planes. Global injectivity preserves disjoint interiors and makes intersections of physical cells precisely the images of the corresponding reference intersections. Their union is the original image. The map, inverse, determinant and finite second-derivative bounds from step 1.2 give all curved-cell requirements [F2]. The reference simplices here are actual parameter simplices; if one instead precomposes with a map from a unit simplex, its Jacobian scaling factors must be retained.

The cell restrictions do not alter the global maps, their physical images, or their value and almost-everywhere derivative differences. Every introduced reference-simplex facet lies in an affine hyperplane, the image of an affine $C^1$ map from $\mathbb R^{d-1}$ into $\mathbb R^d$. By [F4] and [A1] each such hyperplane is null, and the finite union of introduced facets is null. Thus taking essential suprema over the refined interiors gives the same $e_1$; continuity gives the same $e_0$. Since both maps are bi-Lipschitz bijections of the closed box, $G\circ F^{-1}$ is the required homeomorphism between the closed image domains. The within-mesh trace matching in step 2.1 supplies boundary-trace compatibility in [F2]; no exterior trace equality between distinct maps has been proved.

Each normalized ordered-coordinate simplex belongs to a finite set depending only on $d$. Under diagonal scaling, diameter increases by at most $\max_r\ell_r$ and inradius decreases by at most the factor $\min_r\ell_r$ relative to the normalized simplex. Hence the diameter/inradius ratio is at most $\kappa$ times the largest ratio in that fixed finite set. This proves the stated reference shape bound. The remaining uniform curved-map bounds are exactly the additional displayed family assumptions; finite-grid smoothness in step 1.2 supplies only finite-grid constants. No analysis-space change was made in the subdivision.

1. If $|r| < 1$ then $(r^k)$ is **null**, that is $r^k \to 0$
   ([[def-real-limit]]).
2. If $|r| > 1$ then $(|r|^k)$ **diverges to $+\infty$**
   ([[def-divergence-to-infinity]]).

Claim 2 is stated for $|r|^k$ and not for $r^k$ on purpose: for $r < -1$ the
terms $r^k$ alternate in sign and are unbounded, so they neither converge nor
diverge to $+\infty$; what is true of them is the statement about their absolute
values.

Both claims come from Bernoulli's inequality ([[lem-bernoulli-inequality]]) and
the Archimedean property. Nothing here needs the least-upper-bound property
except through [[thm-of-archimedean]] and [[cor-archimedean-reciprocal]].

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.
