The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$, $n\ge p+1$, and $a<b$. A clamped knot vector is a nondecreasing finite sequence
$$\xi_1=\cdots=\xi_{p+1}=a<\xi_{p+2}\le\cdots\le\xi_n<\xi_{n+1}=\cdots=\xi_{n+p+1}=b,$$
with $\xi_j<\xi_{j+p+1}$ for every $1\le j\le n$. Empty interior ranges are omitted. The multiplicity $\mu(\eta)$ of an interior knot $\eta$ is its number of occurrences among $\xi_{p+2},\ldots,\xi_n$.

Write $\mathcal P_p$ for the real polynomials of degree at most $p$. The degree-$p$ spline space $S_{p,\xi}$ consists of functions that restrict to a member of $\mathcal P_p$ on each nonempty knot interval and whose derivatives through order $p-\mu(\eta)$ agree across each interior knot $\eta$. The convention $C^{-1}$ means that no matching condition is imposed. For this piecewise definition, take knot cells left-closed and right-open; at a knot with no matching condition, the value is the one from the cell on its right, and at $b$ use the left limit. Thus the function value at a discontinuous knot is specified.

For each degree $d\in\{0,\ldots,p\}$, the functions $B_{j,d,\xi}$ are indexed by $1\le j\le n+p-d$. Set
$$B_{j,0,\xi}(x)=\mathbf 1_{[\xi_j,\xi_{j+1})}(x),\qquad 1\le j\le n+p.$$
For $1\le d\le p$ and $1\le j\le n+p-d$, define recursively
$$B_{j,d,\xi}(x)=\frac{x-\xi_j}{\xi_{j+d}-\xi_j}B_{j,d-1,\xi}(x)+\frac{\xi_{j+d+1}-x}{\xi_{j+d+1}-\xi_{j+1}}B_{j+1,d-1,\xi}(x),$$
where a term with zero denominator is defined to be zero. For every degree $d$ and every allowed index $j$, set $B_{j,d,\xi}(b)$ equal to its left limit. In particular, the degree-$p$ family has indices $1\le j\le n$. Its basis and regularity properties are proved in [[thm-spline-polynomial-reproduction]].

Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$ and let $\xi$ be a clamped knot vector as in [[def-b-spline-space-and-basis]]. The recursively defined degree-$p$ B-splines are nonnegative, are supported on $[\xi_j,\xi_{j+p+1}]$, and are piecewise polynomials of degree at most $p$. At a knot of multiplicity $\mu\le p$, each B-spline is $C^{p-\mu}$; multiplicity $p+1$ imposes no continuity requirement. On every nonempty knot interval $[\xi_m,\xi_{m+1})$, the active functions $B_{m-p,p,\xi},\ldots,B_{m,p,\xi}$ form a basis of $\mathcal P_p$ and sum to one. Globally, the $n$ B-splines form a basis of $S_{p,\xi}$. In particular, every $q\in\mathcal P_p$ has a unique expansion $q=\sum_{j=1}^n c_jB_{j,p,\xi}$ on $[a,b]$.

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

Assume Countable Choice. Let a bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, be the union of finitely many bounded knot-cell images with disjoint interiors and a face-to-face finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation. Let $m\ge1$ and let $v: \Omega\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^1$ on the closure of each cell, with each component's cell gradient square integrable. Suppose the two one-sided vector values agree on every shared face. Then $v\in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$; its weak gradient is the piecewise classical componentwise gradient. This is the interface condition used to form conforming multipatch isogeometric spaces. Boundary conditions remain an additional restriction such as membership in $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

derivations.claim: The $k=1$ polynomial coefficient formula in [F1] is $x=\sum_i t_iB_i(x)$, while $\sum_iB_i=1$, so $S_rf:=\sum_if(t_i)B_i$ reproduces every affine function. On a cell $(\xi_m,\xi_{m+1})$, all active Greville points lie in $J_m=[\xi_{m-p},\xi_{m+p+1}]\cap[0,1]$, made from at most $2p+1$ nonempty adjacent spans. Nonnegativity and partition of unity give $|S_rf(x)|\le\|f\|_{L^\infty(J_m)}$ for $x$ in that cell. For a $C^1$ section $f$ with $M_g$-Lipschitz derivative, set $T(x)=f(c)+f'(c)(x-c)$ at the left endpoint $c$ of $J_m$. If $y=c$, then $(f-T)(y)=0$; if $y\ne c$, apply [F2] to $f-T$ on the interval with endpoints $c,y$. At the resulting interior point $\zeta$, $|(f-T)(y)|=|f'(\zeta)-f'(c)|\,|y-c|\le M_g|J_m|^2$. At $x\in(\xi_m,\xi_{m+1})$, nonnegativity and partition of unity give $|S_r(f-T)(x)|\le M_g|J_m|^2$. Since $S_rT=T$, $|f(x)-S_rf(x)|\le2M_g|J_m|^2\le2(2p_r+3)^2h_r^2M_g$. Thus each coordinate operator is a sup-norm contraction; the finite operators commute, so the telescoping identity for $I-S_d\cdots S_1$, commutation of different-coordinate operators, and contraction of each $S_r$ let us sum these bounds on the original $g$ and prove the function estimate with $E$.

For one coordinate write $c_i$ for its coefficient, keeping all other Greville samples fixed. Summation of the derivative formula from [F1] gives, on open cells,
$$\left(\sum_ic_iB_{i,p}\right)'=\sum_{\substack{2\le i\le n\\\xi_{i+p}>\xi_i}}\frac{p(c_i-c_{i-1})}{\xi_{i+p}-\xi_i}B_{i,p-1}.$$
Here the nonempty-support lower-degree functions $B_{i,p-1}$, $2\le i\le n$, form a nonnegative partition on each open cell; the two omitted boundary functions vanish there. Terms with $\xi_{i+p}=\xi_i$ are omitted because their lower-degree splines have empty support, so no undefined $0/0$ coefficient is used. Put $\Delta_i=t_i-t_{i-1}=(\xi_{i+p}-\xi_i)/p$. For every included term $\Delta_i>0$, apply [F2] to the coordinate section of $g$ on $[t_{i-1},t_i]$: its derivative quotient $(c_i-c_{i-1})/\Delta_i$ equals $\partial_rg$ at some point between the two Greville samples, with all other coordinates fixed at their samples. If $\Delta_i=0$, then $c_i=c_{i-1}$ and the corresponding lower-degree spline has empty support, so its contribution to the derivative is absent. At a cell point $x$ in the support of an included lower-degree factor, both Greville endpoints lie in $[\xi_i,\xi_{i+p}]$, within $p_rh_r$ of $x_r$; the intermediate point lies there as well. In every other active coordinate, the sample and $x_s$ lie in a common degree-$p_s$ support of length at most $(p_s+1)h_s$. Therefore each gradient value in the nonnegative partition sum is evaluated within distance $R$ of $x$. The $M_g$-Lipschitz gradient yields $|\partial_r\mathcal Sg(x)-\partial_rg(x)|\le M_gR$. Summing squared component bounds proves the gradient estimate.

At an interior knot of multiplicity at most $p$, continuity follows from [F1]. At a knot of multiplicity $p+1$, the left and right pieces are clamped there; the only nonzero endpoint coefficient from each side has Greville point equal to that knot. Their face restrictions are therefore the same tangential sampled sum, so they agree; repeating this argument in each coordinate also gives agreement at intersections of repeated-knot faces. Thus the tensor construction is continuous on the closed box. Its piecewise polynomial gradients are bounded on the finite Cartesian grid, whose rectangular cells form a matching cell partition under the identity map. Under [A1], applying [F3] proves H1 membership and identifies the cell gradients as weak derivatives. The unit box has volume one, so the $L^2$ errors are bounded by the displayed sup bounds. By [F4], $\|g-\mathcal Sg\|_{H^1}=\sqrt{\|g-\mathcal Sg\|_2^2+\|\nabla(g-\mathcal Sg)\|_2^2}\le M_g\sqrt{E^2+dR^2}\le M_g(E+\sqrt d R)$.

At an exterior endpoint of a clamped vector, only its first, respectively last, basis function has value one; the rest are zero. The corresponding Greville point is that endpoint. Substitution into the tensor formula gives exactly the asserted tangential face formula and zero-face preservation. Reflection reverses the knot list and sends each Greville point to $1-t_i$. On open knot cells it reverses the indexed basis functions by the Cox–de Boor recurrence in [F1], starting with the interval indicators. At a fully repeated knot the individual right-cell conventions need not commute with reflection, but the constructed sampled sum is continuous by step 2.1, so equality of the reflected sums on open cells extends to every knot and endpoint. Permuting coordinates merely permutes finite product factors. Consequently aligned face formulas agree under all declared identifications. Constant multiplication commutes with their finite linear sums.

$$\widehat V_h:=\{s/W:s\in S_h\}.$$
Its physical push-forward is $\{\,\widehat v\circ F^{-1}:\widehat v\in\widehat V_h\,\}$. The homogeneous-Dirichlet conforming space is the subspace of these functions that belongs to $H^1_0(\Omega)$; the unconstrained conforming version is the subspace belonging to $H^1(\Omega)$. These spaces are finite dimensional because the tensor B-spline coefficient set is finite.

For vector-valued elasticity in $\mathbb R^d$, use the componentwise product $\widehat V_h^{\,d}:=(\widehat V_h)^d$, push it forward component by component, and intersect with $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ or $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ as appropriate. This remains finite dimensional because it is a subspace of the finite product of scalar coefficient spaces. Trace equality is required componentwise on each shared full face.

For finitely many matching patches, use one such local rational space on each patch. A global trial function is a piecewise physical function whose traces agree pointwise on every shared full face and which belongs to the chosen global $H^1$ or $H^1_0$ space. Under [[def-countable-choice|Countable Choice]], the vector-valued trace-matching lemma [[lem-matching-nurbs-patch-traces-give-h1-conformity]] proves the H1 part of this interface rule componentwise, including the Cartesian product used for elasticity. Nonmatching interfaces are excluded; a mortar or Nitsche method requires a separate stability and consistency result.

The refinement labels have the following meanings.

- **h-refinement** inserts a new knot into a nonempty span at fixed degree and updates homogeneous control data by [[alg-single-new-b-spline-knot-insertion]]. Theorem [[thm-homogeneous-nurbs-knot-insertion-preserves-patch-geometry]] proves exact map preservation for this operation.
- **p-refinement** raises a coordinate degree and replaces the homogeneous representation only when an exact representation with positive new weights is supplied. A degree label alone does not certify geometry preservation or an approximation rate.
- **k-refinement** raises degree and chooses knot multiplicities to obtain a declared continuity, commonly the maximal $C^{p_r-1}$ continuity at simple interior knots. Exact geometry preservation requires the same positive homogeneous representation check as p-refinement.

On each cell, the pullback of scalar gradients and of the linear-elasticity strain is computed using [[lem-isogeometric-pullback-energy-norm-equivalence]]. Exact geometry does not assert exact quadrature. A discretization using an approximate map or quadrature must retain its separate form and load defects.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. On $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]) define $$(u,v)_{H^1}:=(u,v)_{L^2}+\sum_{i=1}^n(D_iu,D_iv)_{L^2},$$ with the $L^2$ inner product of [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. Then $(\cdot,\cdot)_{H^1}$ is an inner product on the Sobolev classes whose induced norm is the $W^{1,2}$ norm of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and $H^1(\Omega)$ is a Hilbert space for it. The zero-boundary space $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a closed subspace of $H^1(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]) and hence a Hilbert space for the restricted inner product. The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, in the convention of [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]].

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space and let
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ be linear in its first argument, conjugate-linear
in its second, bounded by $M$, and coercive with constant $\alpha>0$:
$$|a(v,w)|\le M\|v\|_V\|w\|_V,\qquad \operatorname{Re}a(v,v)\ge\alpha\|v\|_V^2.$$
Let $F:V\to\mathbb K$ be bounded and conjugate-linear, and let $V_h\subseteq V$
be finite-dimensional. Then there are unique $u\in V$ and $u_h\in V_h$ with
$$a(u,v)=F(v)\quad(v\in V).$$
$$a(u_h,v_h)=F(v_h)\quad(v_h\in V_h).$$
The solutions satisfy
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\frac M\alpha\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_V.$$
The real bilinear case uses linear functionals and reads $\operatorname{Re}$ as
the identity.

On $[0,1]^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, choose in coordinate $r$ any finite clamped knot vector $\Xi_r=(\xi^{(r)}_i)$ of degree $p_r\ge1$, with interior multiplicity at most $p_r+1$. Let $h_r$ be its maximum positive span length, $B^{(r)}_i$ its canonical degree-$p_r$ basis, and $t^{(r)}_i=p_r^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{p_r}\xi^{(r)}_{i+k}$ its Greville points. For a real-valued $g\in C^1([0,1]^d)$ with $M_g$-Lipschitz gradient, define the actual tensor comparison spline
$$\mathcal Sg(x)=\sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}g(t^{(1)}_{i_1},\ldots,t^{(d)}_{i_d})\prod_{r=1}^d B^{(r)}_{i_r}(x_r).$$
Put
$$R=\left(\sum_{r=1}^d(p_r+1)^2h_r^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad E=2\sum_{r=1}^d(2p_r+3)^2h_r^2,\qquad B=E+\sqrt d\,R.$$
Then $\mathcal Sg$ is a continuous tensor spline, including at fully repeated knots, and
$$\|g-\mathcal Sg\|_{L^\infty}\le M_gE,\qquad \|\nabla(g-\mathcal Sg)\|_{L^\infty(\mathrm{cells})}\le\sqrt d\,M_gR.$$
For the Sobolev conclusion assume Countable Choice. Then $\mathcal Sg\in H^1((0,1)^d)$ and $\|g-\mathcal Sg\|_{H^1}\le M_gB$. The finite construction, pointwise cell bounds, continuity and face identities do not use this additional choice assumption.
The operator restricts on a coordinate face to the same construction in the tangential coordinates applied to the face data. Thus it preserves zero face data. If two face grids/degrees agree after coordinate permutation and coordinate reflections $t\mapsto1-t$, their face operators agree under that identification and commute with multiplication of the face data by a constant. No knot-ratio bound is needed. All degree and continuity dependence is retained through the actual knots and the displayed degree factors. This comparison operator need not be idempotent.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F:\widehat\Omega\to\Omega$ be an admissible NURBS map and $W$ its continuous denominator, with $W\ge w_->0$ and cellwise $G_W:=\|\nabla W\|_{L^\infty}<\infty$. Let $\widehat u$ be real-valued and let $s\in S_h$ be a real numerator spline; assume both are $C^1$ up to the boundary of each cell in the common refinement of the geometry and analysis knot grids, with matching traces, and put $g:=W\widehat u$. Then the physical rational spline $v_h:=(s/W)\circ F^{-1}$ belongs to $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and
$$\|u-v_h\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C_F C_W\|g-s\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)},\qquad C_F:=\sqrt{j_+}\sqrt{1+L^2},\quad C_W:=\frac{2}{w_-}+\frac{G_W}{w_-^2},$$
where $u:=\widehat u\circ F^{-1}$. This result transfers a specified numerator approximation bound; it does not assert a polynomial-degree-independent rate or a general $H^1$ rate for arbitrary knot families.

Assume Countable Choice. Let a bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, be the union of finitely many bounded knot-cell images with disjoint interiors and a face-to-face finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation. Let $m\ge1$ and let $v: \Omega\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^1$ on the closure of each cell, with each component's cell gradient square integrable. Suppose the two one-sided vector values agree on every shared face. Then $v\in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$; its weak gradient is the piecewise classical componentwise gradient. This is the interface condition used to form conforming multipatch isogeometric spaces. Boundary conditions remain an additional restriction such as membership in $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be open and let $z\in H^1(U)$ vanish almost everywhere outside a compact set $K\subset U$. Then $z\in H^1_0(U)$, where $H^1_0(U)$ is the $H^1$ closure of $C_c^\infty(U)$.

Under the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]], a finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of a nonempty bounded open $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, consists of compact faces $S_1,\ldots,S_q$ covering its boundary, each a compact Borel subset of a regular $C^1$ hypersurface patch, and a compact edge set $E\subset\partial\Omega$. Require $S_j\cap E$ to have surface measure zero in each face, using [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]. E contains the boundaries of the faces relative to their patches and every overlap $S_i\cap S_j$, i different from j. At every point outside E the domain boundary is locally a single $C^1$ graph with Omega on one side. Each face carries this actual outward unit normal off E. Values assigned to the normal on E do not affect its integral.

For a specified finite gluing also list the open pieces with disjoint interiors, the shared faces, and their opposite outward normals. Require the pieces to cover the final domain up to their boundary faces, and the exposed faces to give its specified presentation. Internal faces are counted twice before cancellation, once from each side. The phrase piecewise smooth by itself supplies none of this data.

Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let the reference patch be $\widehat\Omega=(0,1)^d$. For each coordinate $r$, fix a degree $p_r\in\mathbb N_0$, a finite clamped knot vector $\Xi_r$ on $[0,1]$, and its one-dimensional B-spline basis $B^{(r)}_{i_r,p_r,\Xi_r}$ from [[def-b-spline-space-and-basis]]. For a multi-index $\alpha=(i_1,\ldots,i_d)$ in the finite product index set $\mathcal I$, define the tensor-product basis function
$$N_\alpha(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d):=\prod_{r=1}^d B^{(r)}_{i_r,p_r,\Xi_r}(\xi_r).$$

Choose finitely many control points $P_\alpha\in\mathbb R^d$ and positive weights $w_\alpha$, and write $0<w_-:=\min_\alpha w_\alpha\le\max_\alpha w_\alpha=:w_+<\infty$. The weight denominator, rational basis, and associated rational spline space are
$$W(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}w_\alpha N_\alpha(\xi),\qquad R_\alpha(\xi):=\frac{w_\alpha N_\alpha(\xi)}{W(\xi)},\qquad \mathcal N_h:=\operatorname{span}\{R_\alpha:\alpha\in\mathcal I\}.$$
The corresponding NURBS geometry map is
$$F(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}R_\alpha(\xi)P_\alpha.$$
Equivalently, let $\widetilde F(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}(w_\alpha P_\alpha,w_\alpha)N_\alpha(\xi)\in\mathbb R^{d+1}$ and let $\Pi(y,z):=y/z$ for $z>0$. Then $F=\Pi\circ\widetilde F$ wherever $W>0$.
The basis properties in [[thm-spline-polynomial-reproduction]] give nonnegative tensor factors summing to one. Consequently the weights' convex combination satisfies $W\ge w_->0$; the later item `lem-positive-nurbs-basis-and-quotient-derivative` records the full rational-basis consequences.

An admissible NURBS patch map is a continuous, globally injective, bi-Lipschitz map $F:\overline{\widehat\Omega}\to\overline\Omega$ whose restriction to every nonempty knot cell is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism onto its image. There are constants $0<j_-\le j_+<\infty$ and $1\le L<\infty$ such that, almost everywhere on every cell,
$$j_-\le J_F:=\det DF\le j_+,\qquad \|DF\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L,\qquad \|DF^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L.$$
The physical image $\Omega$ is required to be a bounded Lipschitz domain. The images of the finite knot cells form a face-to-face partition with the piecewise $C^1$ boundary presentation of [[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]]; the map agrees on each shared cell face.

A finite multipatch geometry consists of finitely many such patch maps with disjoint physical interiors, a connected bounded Lipschitz union, and matching full physical faces wherever two patches meet. Positive weights only define a positive denominator and a convex rational basis; they do not assert global injectivity, positive Jacobian, or interface matching. Exact NURBS representation means exact representation of the specified CAD map and does not assert that this map is the exact geometry of a target physical domain.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let

$$\mathbb R^{m+n}=\mathbb R^m \times \mathbb R^n,$$
the Lebesgue measure $\lambda_{m+n}$ is the completion of the product measure
$\lambda_m \times \lambda_n$.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single

$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, be bounded, connected, and Lipschitz, and let $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R)$ with norm $\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(D)}$. Let $A:D\to\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ be measurable and symmetric, with constants $0<\alpha\le\beta<\infty$ such that
$$\zeta\cdot A(x)\zeta\ge\alpha|\zeta|^2\quad\text{and}\quad\|A(x)\|_{\rm op}\le\beta\quad\text{for a.e. }x\in D,\ \zeta\in\mathbb R^d.$$
For $f\in V'$, define $a(u,v)=\int_D A\nabla u\cdot\nabla v$ and $F(v)=f(v)$. Let $V_h\subset V$ be any finite conforming isogeometric subspace on the exact admissible patch geometry. Then the weak problem and its Galerkin restriction have unique solutions $u$ and $u_h$, and
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_V.$$
This is an exact-form estimate; it makes no assertion about approximate geometry, quadrature, polynomial-degree-independent constants, or a rate without a separate numerator approximation theorem.

Assume Countable Choice and the real displacement formulation of [[def-linear-elasticity-displacement-formulation-and-data]] on a nonempty bounded, connected Lipschitz domain $D\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$. Let $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ with the gradient norm, let the measurable shear modulus satisfy $0<\mu_0\le\mu(x)\le\mu_1<\infty$ almost everywhere, let $0\le\lambda<\infty$, and let $f\in V'$. For a finite conforming isogeometric subspace $V_h\subset V$ built from the matching NURBS patches of [[def-isogeometric-galerkin-patch-space-and-refinement]], the elasticity variational problem has a unique solution $u$, the Galerkin problem has a unique solution $u_h$, and
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\frac{2\mu_1+d\lambda}{\mu_0}\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_V.$$
The estimate is for each finite $\lambda$ and has a factor growing with $\lambda$; it is not a locking-free or $\lambda$-uniform NURBS result.

Assume Countable Choice and use real scalar Sobolev spaces. Let $\widehat\Omega=(0,1)^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, and $V=H^1_0(\widehat\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with the gradient norm. Let $F$ be an exact admissible patch map and $G$ an approximate admissible map on the same reference box, with a common finite refinement of their cell grids. Let $f$ be a bounded real-linear functional on $H^1_0(F(\widehat\Omega);\mathbb R)$ equipped with its physical gradient norm, and define the exact pulled-back unit-diffusion form and load by
$$\widehat a_F(v,w)=\int_{\widehat\Omega}K_F\nabla v\cdot\nabla w,\quad K_F=(\det DF)DF^{-1}DF^{-\mathsf T},\qquad \widehat\ell_F(w)=\langle f,w\circ F^{-1}\rangle.$$
Define $\widehat a_G$ by the same tensor formula with $G$. Let $u\in V$ solve $\widehat a_F(u,w)=\widehat\ell_F(w)$ for every $w\in V$. Let $V_h\subset V$ be a finite conforming rational spline space and let bounded $a_h$ and $\ell_h$ be a discrete form and load assembled using $G$ and a specified quadrature rule. Assume $a_h$ is coercive on $V_h$ with inherited norm and constant $\alpha_h>0$, and let $M_F$ be a boundedness constant for $\widehat a_F$. Define
$$\delta_{\rm geom}(v_h):=\sup_{w_h\ne0}\frac{|\widehat a_F(v_h,w_h)-\widehat a_G(v_h,w_h)|}{\|w_h\|_V},\quad \delta_{\rm quad}(v_h):=\sup_{w_h\ne0}\frac{|\widehat a_G(v_h,w_h)-a_h(v_h,w_h)|}{\|w_h\|_V},$$
and $\delta_{\rm load}:=\sup_{w_h\ne0}|\widehat\ell_F(w_h)-\ell_h(w_h)|/\|w_h\|_V$. When $V_h=\{0\}$ define all three defects to be zero. Let $u_h\in V_h$ solve the discrete problem; then
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\left((1+M_F/\alpha_h)\|u-v_h\|_V+\frac{\delta_{\rm geom}(v_h)+\delta_{\rm quad}(v_h)+\delta_{\rm load}}{\alpha_h}\right).$$
If $\delta=\|DF-DG\|_{L^\infty({\rm op})}$ and both map derivative and inverse bounds are at most $M\ge1$, then the geometry defect obeys
$$\delta_{\rm geom}(v_h)\le(dM^{d+1}+2M^{d+3})\delta\,\|v_h\|_V.$$
The hypotheses require discrete coercivity; neither exact geometry nor positive NURBS weights imply it. The estimate retains the load defect and makes no convergence claim for any geometry or quadrature rule.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$, let $\mathbb{R}^n$ be the set of functions
$n \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $d_2$ be the Euclidean metric on it
([[lem-metrics-on-rn]]). Then:

1. **Closed boxes are compact.** For reals $a_k \le b_k$ $(k < n)$ the box
   $Q = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_k \le x_k \le b_k \text{ for every } k < n \,\}$
   is a compact subset of $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ ([[def-metric-compactness]]).
2. **Heine-Borel.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ if and only if $K$ is closed in $\mathbb{R}^n$
   ([[def-metric-topology]]) and bounded
   ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]).
3. **The real line.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}, d_{\mathbb{R}})$, the usual metric $d_{\mathbb{R}}(x,y) = |x-y|$
   ([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]), if and only if $K$ is closed in
   $\mathbb{R}$ and bounded.

**No choice principle is used.** The bisection below halves one coordinate at a
time and takes the **left** half whenever the left half still fails to be finitely
covered, the right half otherwise: a rule with two outcomes, decided by a
property of the box, not a selection. That is the whole reason the theorem is
available in ZF, while the general "complete and totally bounded implies compact"
([[thm-complete-and-totally-bounded-implies-compact]]) is not.

The hypothesis $n \ge 1$ is inherited from [[lem-metrics-on-rn]], which defines
$\mathbb{R}^n$ and its metrics only there; the last remark below records what
happens at $n = 0$.

Let $n \ge 1$ and **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]). Then:

1. $\lambda_n$ is sigma-finite ([[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]):
   the cubes $(-k,k]^n$ are Lebesgue measurable with
   $\lambda_n\big((-k,k]^n\big) = (2k)^n < +\infty$, they increase with $k$, and
   their union over $k \in \mathbb{N}$ is $\mathbb{R}^n$.
2. Every bounded subset $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$
   ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]) has $\lambda_n^*(E) < +\infty$; a bounded
   Lebesgue measurable set therefore has finite measure, and every compact
   subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is Lebesgue measurable of finite measure.

On the set of pairs $(a,b)$ with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $b \ne 0$, define

$$(a,b) \sim (c,d) \iff ad = cb \quad \text{in } \mathbb{Z}.$$

This is an equivalence relation ([[lem-rat-equivalence]]). The **rationals** are
the quotient $\mathbb{Q}$, and $[(a,b)]$ is written $a/b$.

Write $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ for the image of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\mathbb{R}$
under the canonical embedding $q \mapsto \hat q$ ([[lem-rat-embeds-dense]]), the
set usually written $\mathbb{Q}$ once the identification is made, and put
$X := \mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ for the irrationals. Then:

1. $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$, that is,
   $\overline{\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}} = \mathbb{R}$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]);
2. $X$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$;
3. every nonempty open subset of $\mathbb{R}$ is uncountable
   ([[def-countable]]).

Claim 2 is not a symmetry of claim 1: the rationals are dense because they are
*constructed* to approximate, whereas the irrationals are dense because there are
too many points in any interval for a countable set to exhaust it, which is why
claim 3 is proved alongside and used for it.

$\mathbb{Q} \approx \mathbb{N}$ ([[def-equinumerous]]): the rationals are
countably infinite ([[def-countable]]).

**No choice principle is used.** The one place where a reader expects a choice,
"pick a representative $a/b$ of each rational", is exactly where
[[lem-rat-positive-denominator]] applies: every rational *has* a representative
with positive denominator, so the map $(a,b) \mapsto [(a,b)]$ defined on
$\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ is already **surjective** onto $\mathbb{Q}$,
and countability follows from a surjection without ever selecting a
representative. The same device handles $\mathbb{Z}$, which is a surjective image
of $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ by construction ([[def-integers]]).

If $A$ and $B$ are at most countable ([[def-countable]]) then so is
$A \times B$.

**No choice principle is used**: the two enumerations are given, and the
enumeration of the product is written down from them.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $P^m$ and $N^n$ be smooth manifolds with $m<n$, and let $F:P\to N$ be a
$C^1$ map. Then $F(P)\subseteq N$ is a null subset of $N$.

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

derivations.claim: On $H=H^1_0(D)$ use its full H1 inner product from [F1] as the coercive form $a_0$, and use the functional $v\mapsto(u,v)_{H^1}$. By [F12], this functional is bounded by $\|u\|_{H^1}\|v\|_{H^1}$; the form $a_0$ has boundedness and coercivity constants both one. Under [A1], [F2] applies; its continuous solution is $u$ itself and its unique discrete solution is precisely the specified $\Pi_hu$. The $M/\alpha=1$ estimate proves the asserted best-approximation bound. The variational equations and uniqueness imply real linearity. If $u\in V_h$, $u$ satisfies the discrete equations, so $\Pi_hu=u$; this proves both surjectivity onto $V_h$ and idempotence, including the zero-space case. Testing with $v_h=\Pi_hu$ and [F12] gives $\|\Pi_hu\|_{H^1}^2\le\|u\|_{H^1}\|\Pi_hu\|_{H^1}$, hence contraction after division when nonzero. All images lie in $V_h\subset H^1_0(D)$.

Put $s_a=\mathcal S_ag_a$. By [F3], it belongs to the actual numerator space, is continuous and cellwise polynomial, and vanishes on exterior faces. On a shared face its two traces obey $s_a=c_{ab}s_b\circ T_{ab}$, because [F3] restricts to the identical tangential construction and respects multiplication by $c_{ab}$. Dividing by the stated denominator relation gives equality of the rational traces. Therefore the piecewise physical $v_h$ has matching values everywhere and continuous value zero on $\partial D$; positivity of the denominator and admissibility of the finite maps make it continuous on $\overline D$, cellwise C1, and give square-integrable gradients. By [F5], $v_h\in H^1(D)$.

On any such box, for each fixed choice of the other coordinates the function of $x_j$ is differentiable. If $z=0$ and $\partial_jz
e0$ at $x_j=t_0$, the derivative definition gives $|z(t)-z(t_0)|\ge 	frac12|\partial_jz(t_0)|\cdot|t-t_0|$ for all sufficiently close $t

e0\}$ is null. The set is measurable on the box because $z$ and $\partial_jz$ are continuous; Fubini [F6] makes $Z_j$ null there.

In the single reference box, write $q:=g-\mathcal Sg$. Directly, $\|q/W\|_{L^2}\le w_-^{-1}\|q\|_{L^2}$ and $\|\nabla(q/W)\|_{L^2}\le w_-^{-1}\|\nabla q\|_{L^2}+G w_-^{-2}\|q\|_{L^2}$ by the quotient rule and the stated lower and derivative bounds for $W$. Thus $\|q/W\|_{H^1}\le(2/w_-+G/w_-^2)\|q\|_{H^1}\le\widehat\varepsilon_h$ by [F3]. This is the direct reference-domain quotient bound.

Each partition face is contained in the image of an incident reference-cell face under its cell expression. The full cell derivative is nonsingular by admissibility, so its restriction to the $(d-1)$-dimensional face tangent space has rank $d-1$; since the rational cell expression extends $C^1$ across that closed face, the face is contained in the image of a $C^1$ map from an open subset of $\mathbb R^{d-1}$. By [F11] each such image, and hence each face, is Lebesgue null. Countably many boxes, finitely many cells, and these null faces show that $\nabla z=0$ almost everywhere on $\{z=0\}$.

Choose a fixed $C^1$ function as follows: let $\chi(t)=0$ for $t\le1$, $\chi(t)=3(t-1)^2-2(t-1)^3$ for $1<t<2$, and $\chi(t)=1$ for $t\ge2$, and set $\theta(s)=s\chi(|s|)$. Then $\theta=0$ on $[-1,1]$, $\theta(s)=s$ for $|s|\ge2$, and $\|\theta'\|_\infty<\infty$. Put $z_\epsilon=\epsilon\theta(z/\epsilon)$. Its cellwise chain rule and matching values give $z_\epsilon\in H^1(D)$ by [F5], with gradient $\theta'(z/\epsilon)\nabla z$. Its support lies in $K_\epsilon:=\{x\in\overline D:|z(x)|\ge\epsilon\}$, which is compact by [F9] and disjoint from $\partial D$; hence $K_\epsilon\Subset D$ and [F5] gives $z_\epsilon\in H^1_0(D)$. The function error is bounded by $C_\theta\epsilon$ for $C_\theta:=\max_{|s|\le2}|\theta(s)-s|$, so its $L^2$ norm tends to zero because $|D|<\infty$ by [F9]. The gradient error tends pointwise to zero off $\{z=0\}$, is zero almost everywhere on that set by step 2.1, and is bounded in squared magnitude by $(1+\|\theta'\|_\infty)^2|\nabla z|^2\in L^1(D)$. Dominated convergence [F6] proves $z_\epsilon\to z$ in $H^1(D)$. Since $H^1_0(D)$ is closed by [F1], $z\in H^1_0(D)$. Applying this result to $v_h$ from step 1.2 gives $v_h\in V_h$.

Apply [F4] on each patch with numerator target $g_a$ and comparison $s_a$, whose required trace and cell regularity were checked in step 1.2. The denominator is continuous by the Statement; its positive cellwise polynomial expression and the closed-box C1 target $g_a$ make $g_a/W_a$ C1 up to every cell boundary, and [A1] supplies Countable Choice. Then [F3] gives $\|u-v_h\|_{H^1(D_a)}\le C_aM_aB_a$. The disjoint patch interiors cover $D$ up to their null faces; the global weak derivatives agree with the local derivatives by [F5]. Sum the squares of these H1 bounds to obtain $\|u-v_h\|_{H^1(D)}\le\varepsilon_h$. Step 1.1 then gives the projector error. Since $h_{a,r}\le1$, the formula for $B_a$ is of order maximum span for fixed degrees; no neighboring-span ratio was used. Varying-degree convergence follows exactly when the displayed upper bound tends to zero.

Use $v_h\in V_h$ from step 3.1 in the best-gradient infimum of [F7] and bound its gradient error by its H1 error from step 4.1. This yields $(\beta/\alpha)\varepsilon_h$ for scalar elliptic data. Apply the same scalar construction to each displacement component; summing the component squared errors replaces $M_a^2$ by $\sum_qM_{a,q}^2$ and gives a conforming vector comparison. The elasticity branch of [F7] then yields the displayed finite-Lamé bound with its existing factor.

On the reference box let $w_h:=\mathcal Sg/W$. The same continuity, quotient and zero-boundary arguments of steps 1.2 and 3.1, with the identity as physical map, put $w_h$ in the reference rational space $V_h\subset H^1_0(\widehat\Omega)$. Step 1.4 proves $\|u-w_h\|_{H^1}\le\widehat\varepsilon_h$. Apply step 1.1 to the reference-domain projector: its best-approximation property gives $\|u-\Pi_hu\|_{H^1}\le\|u-w_h\|_{H^1}\le\widehat\varepsilon_h$. In [F8] choose the admissible comparison $\Pi_hu$ instead of taking the infimum; its gradient error is bounded by this H1 error. This proves the displayed Strang estimate without suppressing any defect. Finally [F8] bounds the geometry defect by the existing tensor constant times $\|DF-DG\|_\infty\|\Pi_hu\|_\nabla$, and step 1.1 gives $\|\Pi_hu\|_\nabla\le\|\Pi_hu\|_{H^1}\le\|u\|_{H^1}$.
